members.title: 这次和好友分手种田！多人混乱新作《嗨斗农场》今日登陆主机平台

news.body:
Cloth Cat Games与Curveball Games今日宣布，混乱欢乐的多人游戏《嗨斗农场》（Planted!）现已登陆PlayStation 5及Xbox Series X|S，PC版即将推出。玩家将走进菜园——当然，还有火山、山坡以及百分之百正常的农场——与好友展开园艺对决。玩家需要播种、种植，再把刚收获的农产品扔向目标或对手，争取拿下更多分数，成为最终冠军。
从狂风肆虐的山坡、幽深的洞穴，到尚未完工的摩天大楼和活火山，没有哪处地方偏远或危险到能阻止这些园艺新手大展身手。游戏中的八个多人竞技场各有独特挑战，玩家将在其中争夺排行榜上的高位与最终胜利。
不过，剥洋葱的方法可不止一种。玩家还能使用各种强化道具，想方设法压过对手，包括杂草炸弹、土豆炮塔，以及诡异的绿色克隆体！
除了八个各具特色的多人竞技场外，《嗨斗农场》还提供独立的单人剧情模式，带玩家深入竞争激烈的园艺世界。玩家将前往不同地点，接受精彩挑战并迎战强大的头目，检验自己的竞技园艺实力。单人战役中掌握的技巧也能自然运用到多人对战中。
Cloth Cat Games创意制作人 Ben Cawthorne 表示：
“我们非常激动《嗨斗农场》今天终于登陆主机平台，PC版也即将推出！最初，这只是一个供我们试验各种古怪点子的有趣原型；如今，它已经成为整个团队倾注了大量心血的作品。我们迫不及待想看到玩家和朋友们展开疯狂的园艺对决，也希望大家在尝试不同战术、把自己种出来的农产品扔出去争取高分时玩得开心！”
Curveball Games高级发行经理 Ed Gregory 表示：
“游戏发售总是一个重要的里程碑，而Cloth Cat团队为《嗨斗农场》打造了一款特别的作品——这正是那种适合和朋友一起打开、然后互相扔巨大胡萝卜的游戏。当然，想扔洋葱也可以，由你们决定。”
《嗨斗农场》现已推出PlayStation 5及Xbox Series X|S数字版，PC版即将推出。PlayStation 5实体版计划于圣诞节前发售。Nintendo Switch数字版将于2027年初推出，实体版也计划于2027年发售。

members.title: 《刺客信条》2026秋季更新

news.body:
秋季已至，我们想和大家聊聊自2026年3月“《刺客信条》：迈向2026”发布之后，《刺客信条》系列正在推进的工作与未来计划。内容负责人 Jean Guesdon 将带大家了解近期的系列动态，以及接下来值得期待的内容。 让我们先从总体情况聊起。 共建《刺客信条》的未来 如果你错过了此前的消息：我们已于今年早些时候公布了全新的《刺客信条》领导团队。该团队由来自系列不同领域的资深成员组成，职责是塑造《刺客信条》的未来，并确保这一系列在未来数年保持连贯统一的整体方向。 该团队由 Martin Schelling 领导。过去数月中，团队一直在为下一阶段的发展打下基础，细化长期愿景，并明确关键优先事项。 虽然我们目前还无法透露具体细节，但希望再次强调指导这项工作的原则： · 忠于《刺客信条》独一无二的核心特质 · 持续推动创新 · 打造多样化的游戏体验 · 提升游戏品质与内容一致性 在构建系列未来的同时，我们也希望持续与你们保持沟通。 与社区建立更紧密的联系 今年3月，我们通过社区问卷邀请玩家分享对《刺客信条》未来的看法。数千名玩家参与其中，告诉了我们他们最在意的内容，感谢大家的参与！ 从反馈中可以看出，以下方向尤为重要： · 希望《刺客信条》能够继续保留其独有特色与核心要素 · 期待游戏拥有更连贯的叙事体验，并且让游戏尊重和拓展《刺客信条》的世界观与故事 · 希望我们能与社区保持更频繁、更稳定的沟通 这些反馈与领导团队内部正在进行的讨论不谋而合。正如前文所提到的，提升整个系列及其世界观设定的一致性是我们的重点工作之一。 我们也将继续通过多种方式与大家分享动态，而像这样的更新就是其中之一。 为了持续倾听社区声音，我们计划在今年举办多场闭门交流活动，邀请核心社区成员与内容创作者参与，让玩家反馈能够更直接地传递至开发团队。我们始终在寻找新的声音，如果你希望获得未来的参与机会，请在官方社交频道保持活跃。 这些交流活动能帮助我们深入讨论特定话题，但我们同样希望听到整个社区的想法。因此，新一轮社区问卷调查现已开放。 欢迎花几分钟分享你的意见，与我们一起塑造《刺客信条》的未来。 接着，让我们来看看现有游戏的最新动态。 现有游戏更新 《刺客信条：黑旗 记忆重置》最终重大更新 这大概是历史上最不是秘密的秘密……而现在，它终于成真了！《刺客信条：黑旗 记忆重置》已于7月9日发售。看到如此多玩家再次掌舵寒鸦号，我们感到无比欣喜。 过去数月中，育碧新加坡团队持续通过体验优化更新与新增内容改进游戏体验。如今，游戏的最终重大更新已经到来，带来以下内容： · 新游戏+ · 噩梦模式 · 全新奖励 · 全新终结动作 · 全新饰品 · 更多自定义选项 新奖励中还包括专为社区准备的惊喜内容：黑胡子的标志性外观、爱德华的伦敦服装，以及适用于寒鸦号和船员的全新自定义选项。 这次更新也标志着我们当前针对《刺客信条：黑旗 记忆重置》追加大型内容计划的结束。希望它能再给你一个重返加勒比海、征服大海的理由。 不过，还有另一个地方等待你扬帆启航…… “新游戏+”即将加入《刺客信条：英灵殿》 《刺客信条：英灵殿》玩家人数已于近期突破4000万。为庆祝这一里程碑，我们将带来社区呼声极高、也等待已久的功能：“新游戏+”将于11月5日上线。
无论你想重新体验艾沃尔的传奇、尝试新的构筑，还是带着心爱的装备再次征服英格兰，“新游戏+”都能让你在继承大量成长进度的同时开启全新旅程，并提供专属的“新游戏+”升格调整。 本次“新游戏+”更新还将加入： · 一项可选成长模式：装备、符文与特长都将共同影响艾沃尔的总体强度 · 全新符文、成就、储藏系统与奖励 · 全新大师刺客外观，设计灵感来自《刺客信条：影》中奈绪江的造型 · 秘银：用于升级神圣装备并强化符文的全新资源 · 所有物品开放神圣装备品质 完整内容将在后续的更新日志中公布。未来几天，我们也会分享关于当前世代主机更新的更多信息。 请务必在我们的社交媒体频道参与讨论，分享您对本次新更新的反馈，这将有助于我们未来就将类似更新引入其他《刺客信条》系列作品展开讨论。 开发中的游戏项目 《刺客信条》系列各团队目前正持续推进多个开发中项目。 《代号Invictus》 负责《代号Invictus》——《刺客信条》雄心勃勃的多人游戏项目——的团队在过去这一年过得非常忙碌。 数月前，数百名玩家参与了首轮内部活动，亲手体验游戏早期原型，并直接向开发团队分享反馈。 PvP 多人玩法的回归获得了非常积极的反响。参与者尤其喜欢地图中的跑酷与垂直空间、动态团队协作，以及操控不同《刺客信条》角色的机会——每名角色都拥有独特技能与玩法风格。 不过，有一项反馈尤为明确：玩家认为项目的基础拥有巨大潜力，但希望看到更多定义了《刺客信条》的核心支柱。团队在过去的数月内已据此采取行动，《代号Invictus》正在朝着更好体现这些核心支柱的方向发展，同时仍忠于其多人玩法愿景。 《代号Invictus》仍处于开发阶段，因此玩家在网络上看到的信息可能并不完整、已经过时或不够准确。团队将继续测试新版本，并在准备好分享更多内容后及时更新。 不过，多人游戏并非该系列中唯一正在幕后逐步成形的部分…… 《代号Hexe》 《代号Hexe》将是一段更黑暗的《刺客信条》体验，目前正在稳步推进中，但团队仍有大量工作需要完成。我们知道玩家已经等待很久，感谢大家对这一项目的耐心与持续热情。 团队正专注于实现项目最核心的独特愿景，并将在2027年分享下一次重大更新。 在准备好公布更多信息前，我们也会继续关注大家的想法、讨论与期待，见证这段体验逐渐成形。
关于其他重制作品 我们知道，社区近期一直对重制作品抱有许多疑问——尤其是在《刺客信条：黑旗 记忆重置》推出之后。 作为系列首部重制作品，《刺客信条：黑旗 记忆重置》让我们收获了大量经验。重制一部在玩家心中占据特殊位置的作品，既令人兴奋，也伴随着挑战：从零构建旧系统、加入能够契合体验的新元素，并在传统与创新之间取得平衡，这是一项艰巨的任务。我们对《刺客信条：黑旗 记忆重置》团队所取得的成果以及游戏所收获的积极反响感到无比自豪。 在此，我们想明确说明的一点是，目前我们并没有在研发其他《刺客信条》系列的重制作品。我们的团队已经将精力集中于《刺客信条》的下一篇章，其中包括一些大家尚未听闻的项目，这些项目将呈现全新的背景设定和故事。 但这并不意味着重制的大门已经关上。和许多玩家一样，我们也喜欢重温系列经典作品的想法，并将持续探索让旧作回归的可能。 这扇门依然敞开。毕竟——万物皆虚，万事皆允。
其他项目 Netflix 真人剧集 除了游戏项目外，还有另一项工作正在幕后稳步推进。 Netflix《刺客信条》真人剧集的制作目前正在意大利罗马接近完成。Jean 曾前往剧组探班、参与剧本咨询，并与剧集主创团队交流。 我们近期还公布了一项令人兴奋的消息：获奖作曲家 Hannah Peel （曾为英剧《失眠》、《弗雷加德》及纪录片《权利的游戏：最后的守夜人》等作品创作配乐）已加入该项目，并将负责剧集配乐。 目前尚未公布该剧集发布日期。玩家可前往 Tudum 查看目前已公开的全部信息。在我们真正踏入罗马帝国之前，还请大家和我们一起在暗影中静待一段时间。
即将到来的庆典 最后但同样重要的是：《刺客信条》将在明年迎来20周年！ 这是系列的重要里程碑，我们非常期待与你们共同庆祝。 团队正在筹备一整年的内容，包括全新公布、更新、奖励以及社区活动。我们的计划仍处于严格保密阶段，但可以确定的是：这场周年庆典将以玩家为核心。没有大家的热情、创意和支持，《刺客信条》不会走到今天。 请持续关注官方频道，2027年庆典开启时，我们会与大家分享更多内容。 未来几个月我们还将分享更多内容，在此之前，先来一睹标志着《刺客信条》系列20周年的LOGO吧。
结语 以上就是今天想和大家分享的全部内容。 我们并不总能公布每一个细节，或回答所有问题；打造优秀的游戏需要时间。但我们会持续与你们保持联系，尽我们所能地分享，并继续倾听大家的声音。 感谢你们在日常中分享对《刺客信条》的想法、期待与热爱。 现在，是时候让我们重归暗影了……下次见。 信条永存！<)
想了解更多《刺客信条》的相关信息，请关注育碧官网和育碧官方微博。 |

news.title: 没有放弃！Bungie宣布“社区更新”博客回归
news.summary_raw: Bungie 于日前宣布，“Bungie社区更新”博客正式回归。据悉，该博客不会作为每周固定专栏发布，而是在有实质性内容时不定期更新。团队希望，能第一时间和玩家通报工作室动态以及旗下《命运》和《马拉松》的发展规划。 (此前命运剧情内容回归需要约12个月的时间) 本次博客中，Bungie 产品主管 Josh Deane就《命运2》停服公告后的工作室现状、品牌遗产与未来规划进行了回应。为配合《马拉松》后续的更新，工作室已推出“开发者洞察”系列视频，并计划重启播客、直播与线上答疑等活动。 Josh Deane 指出，重塑与玩家的信任是当前工作的核心，而非靠宣布新规划博取关注。他表示，公布《命运2》停服计划前的几个月是工作室最艰难的时期。面对不确定的未来，Josh Deane 与团队成员 Poria 决定调整运营方向，确保 Bungie 、《命运》与《马拉松》迎来改变。除了剧情内容回归外，团队确认还有更多惊喜，会在适当的时间公布。 在发布凯旋纪念碑及停服公告前夕，Bungie 临时修改了宣传文案与回应基调。工作室希望以此激发社区的凝聚力，而非将其定性为告别仪式。公告发布后，玩家群体积极发起请愿并分享回忆，强烈呼吁保留这一游戏世界。Bungie 表示，玩家的反响为团队提供了持续动力，希望能围绕游戏的共同未来展开探讨。

news.rss_content: Happy Neowlloween, Slayers! Much like last month, this Neowsletter is coming in a little later than usual. But this time it's because we wanted to wait until we were able to offer some more solid info on when you can expect to see the next update. Since August (aside from our 1 week studio break), we've been busy working on some big pieces of content that we've alluded to in past Neowsletters. All of these features were included in our Early Access roadmap at launch, but it wasn't until the past couple of months that we've had the time to concentrate all of our focus on creating them. As you can imagine, these are big things that require a lot of design, UX work, art, animation, balancing, etc before they're even ready for the experimental beta branch. They can't be pumped out in a short amount of time nor can they be efficiently worked on in tandem with regular balance updates and bug fixes. While we mentioned in the August Neowsletter that our next update would take a bit longer, we weren't sure exactly when that would be... until now! The next big beta patch is currently planned to release on November 12th , which is just a couple of weeks away by the time you're reading this. Of course, this new experimental content will be beta-exclusive at first as we work out the kinks, but the default/main branch will be brought up-to-date with all of the content, balance, and fixes that are live on the current and relatively stable beta branch version (v0.111.0). By this time next month, beta players will already have delved deep into the new stuff and will be sharing their opinions on why [REDACTED] should be buffed, [REDACTED] should be nerfed, and so on. The new content will have more of an impact the less we say about it, so we're going to keep those arrows in our quiver for now. By the way... some of the team is heading to Shanghai for WePlay 2026 !! There will be a Slay the Spire 2 booth with demos, exclusive merch, and interactive elements thanks to our friends at CiGA, as well as a Q&A and fan signing event with Casey! If you're in town from November 21-22, we hope to see you there! In the meantime, let's answer some of the community's questions that have been building up over the last while... Q&A with C&A Natalie asks: Loving Slay the Spire 2 so far, thank you so much for all the work you’ve put into it! Would it be possible for you to add modifiers to the custom run mode to force a specific Ancient to spawn at the start of Acts 2 + 3? Or a modifier that lets us pick which version of each act appears, like getting to choose between Overgrowth + Underdocks for Act 1? No worries if this isn’t possible due to coding reasons/it messing with the RNG, or if you just don’t want to add something like this. Casey: We'll likely have to do a pass on Custom Runs near the v1.0 launch. While I want to add all the features and ways to explore the nooks and crannies of the game, controller support and minimum text size requirements make it difficult for us. This likely means that Desktop players + mods will get the most flexibility. Oliwier asks: Hello megacrit team!! I've been wondering, is the yellow thing on the inklet a happy mouth or a single sad eye? Casey: It's a single sad eye :( HJain asks: I was wondering whether the team is currently thinking about long-term difficulty/replayability systems for co-op. Is something similar to Ascension planned or being considered for multiplayer? And are there plans for additional regions or alternative Acts that could make late-game runs more varied? Casey: We've found the reception to co-op really positive so we definitely want to add more longevity to it with many players letting us know that they exclusively play multiplayer too! As for additional Acts, that's certainly in the pipes (within the Spire). goodsoup asks: I have been loving STS2, especially multiplayer. I was wondering if we could get a system for trading gold. I understand why you may not want that for relics/potions, but i would love to be able to give someone else my remaining 23 gold esp. if we are about to fight a boss. Casey: If players can pool their resources to a single player it's sometimes too easy to have one player snowball, which is a growth for characters throughout a run. The ability to get a relic that's more suited for you in Treasure Rooms is already quite advantageous... Jeremy asks: I like how your team has been willing to retune, rework, and modify content from the open access period to really match the vision of what you're going for. With that being said, is there anything that you feel like "dang we really nailed that the first time around"? Anything from content/difficulty/art direction/etc. Thanks! Casey: Bash is the perfect card Nicolas asks: how many feedbacks did you get since the beginning of EA? are you using a tool to cluster similar feedbacks or is this manageable by hand? Casey: The feedback all goes into a tool that we use though. We do a handful of both! The quantity of a specific type of feedback can tell us how frequently the issue occurs while we sometimes look for feedback on a specific card, encounter, etc :) NeonWyvern asks: What is the best way we as players can word our in-game feedback (our F2s)? It must be hard to parse through all that player data, so how can we make our F2s easier for you to work with? Casey: It's not that hard to work with, please keep using the in-game feedback tool. The in-game tool gives us the most data, lets us sort issues by category, helps us not open a ton of emails or hunt down Steam discussions. It's the best way by far! Kale asks: Would you ever be open to the idea of an official story adaptation of Slay the Spire (1 & 2)? Like the games being adapted into a graphic novel or even an animated series with a more cohesive story integrating all the lore and worldbuilding of the Spire and Preon? Casey: Yeah I'm open Jeffreyjelly asks: Have you ever thought about collaborating with other games to create new characters at all? (This does sound like a balancing nightmare to add a bunch of cards though) Anthony: no Aarfdark asks: I've been loving STS 2 so far and I can't wait for what's in store for us next! In the August Neowsletter, you said that y'all were working on experimental game modes. Could you tell us anything along the lines of how many you're planning on making and whether they're going to be focused around single player or multiplayer? Casey: The new game modes will work for both singleplayer and multiplayer but aside from that, you'll have to wait... until November 12th! Peeled Tomato asks: I've been loving Slay The Spire 1 and 2. My question is: Just like in StS 1 we were able to see the Beta Artstyle of cards, will we see them in StS 2 in Cards as well as in the Timeline? (I love the place holder Art in the Timeline that's why!) Anthony: yes Casey: Did you just... say yes? Spire Spotting Last month we shared our discovery of a mysterious creature that our team of researchers had yet to uncover from a mysterious shadow. Today, with the help of all of your hypotheses, we will endeavor to discover its true form! First, a look at the still-shadowed being... And now for some hypothesis highlights. The award for most memey goes to inging for their tiny Doormaker resurrection! The award for most seasonally festive goes to Sophia ! The award for most like an actual field notebook illustration goes to Straight D Student ! The award for most hunger-inducing goes to Fleic ! I wonder if the real thing would be tasty, too... The award for most Defect-ive goes to Ooby ! Throwback to the days of Spire Spotting when people still did not know if the Defect would be making a return to the Spire or what form it would take. And, lastly, the award for most accurate goes to Yendorami ! Minus the eye, you were pretty spot on! We received many, many submissions and we wish we could feature them all, but here is a small selection of others! Credit from left to right: gamingpower9, TheSos, GrayKitten, Mailboy002, Frost, BananaDream, Huntress, Linkerawesomer, Cloutsky, Teh Quiper, tyo, SleeplessS, DextrasDeluge, Blizzkit, Aliza, Soheil. Now with all of your hard work, we're finally able to unshroud this strange creature... AHA! I knew it would be cute!! One couldn't possibly fight such a thing, surely... It seems as though this aquatic creature got lost in this shadowy realm. Perhaps we should return it to the Underdocks? We won't name it, of course, lest we get attached! Thank you once again to everyone who helped in our research of this squishy guy--I mean formidable creature! Perhaps our paths will cross again if we require your assistance in the future. Merch Madness We've had quite a few merch announcements this month and we're rounding them all up here! We're not in the business of making t-shirts or figures, so rest assured that these collabs have taken up zero dev time. While merch does help support our team, the main reason we do it is to make the merch-lovers in our community happy! And to suffocate our community manager with an ever-growing plushie collection. Makeship's Menace Event has brought some spooky, Spire-y plushies along! For a limited time, you can get a real-life, plush Mini Regent (complete with throne and minions) AND a Squeeze-able Necrobinder and matching Osty! Since this Neowsletter came out a bit later and since this may be the only chance to get an official plushie of these guys for a long time, we've extended the pre-order campaign by 1 week past Halloween, until November 7th! The latest Fangamer drop is here! Now you can don this long-sleeved tee featuring resplendent art of the Regent or a charming Neow pin (finally)! Also, you can now rest your keyboard, mouse, and other accoutrement on this fittingly rest site-themed deskmat!! The Slay the Spire collection at The Yetee got some starry and skeletal additions! Show off your love for the Spire's latest slayers with these beautiful brand new prints and tees of the Regent and the Necrobinder! The first ever Slay the Spire x GoodSmile collab is booting up with a Nendoroid Light figure of The Defect! Go wishlist this cute little version of everyone’s favorite robot friend to get notified when it drops!! Mapsterpieces Alright, we finally gave in and renamed this section to Mapsterpieces! If last month's theme was "large," this month's theme has turned out to be "cute." ^-^ A variety of adorable Defects by Maddokun ! Plush Defect and Plush Silent hanging out by MS32 ! A little Hollow Silent by Coffee ! Connections Section While away the time until the next patch with this (maybe) terrifyingly tricky Slay the Spire Connections puzzle ! Mega Crit-or-Treat! BOO!!! Mega Crit-or-Treat has returned from the grave!! As many of you may know, our Discord hosts an annual event where community members can share their spooky Spire creations in exchange for a special limited-time role (this year's is Impish Inklet). This can include fanart, costumes, carvings, anything--as long as it's in the spirit of the season! You still have a few days left if you'd like to participate, so get in on it while you can! Community Corner Thank you to 櫻 ヨル for this month's amazing, spooky cover image! As usual, our community is so talented it's SCARY, so shoutout to these incredible pieces by our runner ups: DotNetIzzy, Tooza, Marr0w, pennypunkos, Ayla, pictoprojects, Joniperita, and 阿星. Next month's theme is: Neow's Bounty! Imagine denizens of the Spire reaping the season's harvest, indulging in a feast, or just enjoying the last remnants of autumn. If you'd like to submit your art for consideration, reminder that it must be submitted to us via fanmail@megacrit.com or in our Discord's fanart channel, have dimensions of 800x450px, feature no text, and leave room for a title! Please make your submission by Sunday, November 15th. On with the monthly community highlights! A cute illustration celebrating the Defect's upcoming figure by pp ! These amazing Minion cosplays courtesy of glorblargh (with a bonus back view)! https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aM6Tfoc8ayc This iconic animation of the minions enjoying pop music by Rixian ! That's all for this month, folks. By the time the next Neowsletter hits your inbox you'll already be enjoying a brand new patch (and we're not talking pumpkins)!

news.title: Xbox CEO says console demand is outstripping supply—but sales continue to drop
news.summary_raw: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma insists that the demand for Xbox consoles is there, Microsoft simple cannot produce enough, a claim that may clash with Xbox's public sales data.

members.title: Xbox CEO says console demand is outstripping supply—but sales continue to drop
Xbox first-party content partially offsets 2% drop in Q1 revenue, hardware decreases 14%

news.body:
At Microsoft's investor call last night, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma spoke about the unit sales of the Xbox, stating that console demand is higher than supply and indicating that players want to buy Xbox units but they are simply not finding any available, later resharing her comments on X (formerly Twitter). But that claim may clash with Microsoft's own financial results.
Sharma's claim is that, for the quarter being reported in these recent financial results, the lower sales of the Xbox compared to previous sales performance, is because they are unable to manufacture or supply enough console units, while also pointing out that the overall decline has lessened between quarters when compared to the previous year.
Beyond Sharma's initial statement, which focuses on revenue, the financial results report that Xbox hardware revenue has fallen 14 percent year over year this quarter, despite the price going up. For demand to be outstripping supply, the hardware revenue should be seeing big gains, not the relatively modest ones shown by the publicly available numbers.
While local stock is always going to vary depending on a number of factors, cursory checks on supply both locally and nationwide does not indicate that Xbox Series X or Series S are particularly difficult to find in retail environments at present, so it is unclear what Sharma means about demand outstripping supply. As prices for the console continue to go up seemingly driven by a global memory shortage, it is possible a spike in demand in anticipation of high-profile releases like Grand Theft Auto VI might be occurring to head off future price increases from the consumer end.
A silver lining on the cloud
These financial results are the first major quarter reported since Xbox's much-vaunted reset, which seeks to get the division back to profitability by cutting jobs across all of Xbox. It may be a little too soon to tell the full effects of cutting 1,600 jobs—with another 1,600 left to go by July 2027—there does not appear to be a meaningful improvement in Xbox's numbers from the large-scale pivot.
As previously mentioned, Xbox content and services revenue was down 2 percent, which saw declines in third-party content and Xbox Game Pass, though the latter may be the direct effects of the April price cut. The Devices and Consumer segment of Microsoft reported that the cost of revenue "declined 8 percent driven by lower amortization of intangible assets from the Activision acquisition." In other words, intangible assets acquired with the purchase of Activision, like trademarks and patents, are assumed to be worth less now than they were when Microsoft acquired the video game publisher.
One bit of good news for the company is that Microsoft Cloud revenue hit a milestone goal of $63.9 billion, accelerating to 30 percent growth year-over-year. Both cloud and AI initiatives are buoying the company overall, pushing it to better numbers over the previous year even as divisions like Xbox continue to drag.

news.body:
由独立游戏发行商Analgesic Productions推出的像素剧情游戏《团地日和》近日在Steam正式发售，游戏首发售价43.2元。
游戏试玩版在之前，就获得了95%好评率特别好评的优秀成绩，正式版故事发生在一个颇有历史的“团地”，即居民区中。你将化身一名少女星乃，为了患有痴呆症的奶奶立志重办团地夏日祭，努力邀请众多个性十足的邻居参加庆典。哪怕遭到拒绝，也可以探索团地和网络，寻找突破口，说服他们参与进来。
小小居民区大冒险
作为一款叙事题材的游戏，《团地日和》温馨可爱的画风之下，讲述了现代社会存在的诸多问题。除了作为关键切入点的，患有老年痴呆的奶奶，玩家还必须在重办夏日祭的过程中，与团地中生活着的各式邻居打交道。其中既有老龄化、少子化社会下，长期独居的老人；也有因为互联网高度普及，而逐渐疏离人群的宅家一族。
神奇邻居在哪里
当然，游戏并不会苦大仇深地讲述社会问题。游戏里出现的所有角色，虽然都存在一定的社会背景，但在12岁小女孩的眼中，他们所展现的形象，却是有趣又独特的神奇邻居。居民阵容共有51人，年龄层横跨12岁至87岁，而且个个性格独特，在邀请他们重办夏日祭的过程中，玩家可以像收集“宝可梦”那样，通过与邻居们建立奇妙联系，来将他们记录在册。
充满童心的小游戏
在攻略这些神奇邻居，以及完成游戏各种挑战的过程中，主角将触发各种小游戏挑战，这些小游戏的创意全部来自于作者童年时，在居民区里与玩伴胡闹时发明的小游戏。你可以通过它们，来体验奶奶在身体硬朗时对星乃的教导：“用五感去感受”。树木散发的清香，雨后积起的水洼……寻找隐藏在团地日常生活中的小游戏，像小时候那样全情投入、尽情嬉戏吧。
游戏《团地日和》现已在Steam正式发售，售价43.2元，感兴趣的玩家不妨在Steam上搜索游戏名 团地日和 就能找到。

news.title: 完美世界2026年Q3扣非净利润4.71亿元创单季近5年新高
news.summary_raw: 完美世界2026年Q3扣非净利润4.71亿元，创近5年单季新高，业绩增长主要得益于自研游戏《异环》的全球表现，电竞、影视业务并进，前瞻布局前沿科技。

members.title: 完美世界2026年Q3扣非净利润4.71亿元创单季近5年新高
完美世界2026年Q3扣非净利润4.71亿元创单季近5年新高

news.body:
上线6个月以来，《异环》不仅稳住了国内基本盘，还成功打开了海外增量。
10月29日，完美世界发布了2026年第三季度报告。公司Q3单季实现营收23.62亿元，同比增长36.85%；归母净利润5.06亿元，扣非净利润4.71亿元。其中，Q3单季度的扣非净利润创下了自2021年Q4以来的最高值。
根据公告披露，今年4月底上线的年度重点产品《异环》，截至10月28日全球累计流水超27亿元人民币，其中全球官方渠道（官方PC+官方安卓）累计流水占比近60%。
值得注意的是，目前《异环》海外累计流水贡献已高于国内市场，也让出海成为此次完美世界三季报的最大看点。
爆款新品发力 出海体系进阶
公告显示，三季报飘红，主要系自研产品《异环》公测带来的收入增量。
根据公开信息，完美世界对《异环》的定位是“全球品质、多端并发”的潮流赛道新代表。从市场端看，《异环》从上线前到公测半年以来，获得了以二次元为核心的广泛玩家群体的高度关注，各类商业联名活动频繁，IP影响力已从游戏内延伸到多元消费场景。
在海外，该产品4月底面向全球180余个国家和地区开启公测以来，在海内外主要区域多次进入iOS游戏畅销榜前五，并在日本等海外市场多次登顶PS主机热门榜。
根据三季报披露，《异环》的国内市场及海外绝大部分区域均由完美世界自主发行。相对于单一产品在海外获得成功，这一自主发行能力的沉淀，是出海叙事中更具长期价值的一环。
游戏业内人士指出，传统出海路径中，研发商多将其交给出海发行商代理，不只是要给发行商分成，对海外市场的穿透力也会受到限制。当产品失利时，厂商甚至难以判断问题出在产品本身还是发行环节。
相比之下，自主发行不仅利润率更高，还可以让厂商把对海外市场的渠道关系、用户数据、本地化运营经验和市场反馈的主动权都握在自己手中，不断积累经验。
完美世界方面表示，从此前多个产品自主出海发行试水，到《异环》全面自主海外发行，公司持续建设自有全球发行能力，未来将依托焕新升级的全球化发行体系为产品赋能。
这意味着，《异环》不只是一款出海产品，更是对海外发行能力的实战演练，这对于侧重研发的完美世界而言具备更多意义，也是观察完美世界下一步出海逻辑是否成立的关键。
利润如期释放 毛利率逆势上行
从财务报表看，由于《异环》上线前期营销推广费用激增带来了压力，今年完美世界半年报形成了账面亏损。
不过，到6月末，代表玩家已充值但尚未消费的递延收入的合同负债总额较年初增长6.07亿元，说明《异环》当时就已经赚到了真金白银，只待利润释放。
此次三季报就给出了符合此前市场预期的答案。前三季度，完美世界的游戏业务实现营收47.92亿元，较上年同期增加7.09%；实现归母净利润4.34亿元，环比扭亏为盈。
公告显示，尽管若干游戏受生命周期影响收入同比下滑，但自研游戏的利润贡献较上年同期稳中有升，长青游戏矩阵仍在持续补充新活力。
从2026年前三季度看，完美世界实现营业收入51.13亿元，归母净利润3.87亿元，扣非净利润2.61亿元，环比半年报顺利扭亏为盈。前三季度公司营业成本较上年同期减少29.39%，经营活动产生的现金流量净流入额为11.81亿元，同比增加32.87%。
营业成本减少、现金流改善的同时，完美世界的毛利率也在提升。
根据公告，公司前三季度综合毛利率69.53%，较上年同期提升10.26个百分点；其中游戏业务毛利率73.79%，较上年同期提升4.5个百分点。
有业内人士指出，游戏厂商毛利率的提升在当前竞争环境中尤为可贵。由于年内新品密集上线，用户时长争夺白热化，加上买量成本高企，而渠道分成长期分走利润，许多游戏厂商的毛利率持续摊薄。
“在这种背景下，完美世界的收入增长与毛利率双双上行，说明其增长来自产品结构优化、自研内容占比提升及成本端的主动收缩，是更健康的质量型增长，”上述人士表示。
电竞影视并进 科技前沿布局
在游戏产品出海之外，电竞正成为完美世界另一条跑通的出海路径。
今年8月，2026 DOTA2国际邀请赛（TI2026）于上海举办，赛事共吸引6万人次到场观赛，其中海外观众1.2万人次，覆盖全球70余个国家和地区。
作为DOTA2国服运营商，这是完美世界继2019年TI9之后再次助推这一顶级赛事落地国内。本次TI赛事，赛场内外融入了大量苏绣、中国民乐等特色文化元素，“电竞+文化”的出海受到了主流媒体与青年用户的广泛认可。
今年9月，2027反恐精英世界锦标赛（上海Major2027）正式官宣重返中国，将由完美世界电竞于2027年四季度在上海主办，此前该赛事曾在2024年由完美世界在上海主办。
通过持续举办全球化高水准赛事，完美世界承接国际顶级电竞赛事落地、组织与本地化运营的能力逐步强化，正在夯实在国内电竞产业的头部地位，并拓宽自身出海路径。
影视方面，前三季度实现营业收入3.07亿元，公司坚持“减量提质”，长剧保持精品创作节奏，同时依托技术能力布局短剧、中剧等新品类。
当前，AI等前沿技术加速推动内容研发模式升级，行业竞争重心正从规模资源转向创意能力。完美世界持续落实“技术赋能”战略，紧抓创新技术研发与前沿技术应用，以技术创新让内容创意落地生根，更好地服务于用户体验。
得益于其在游戏业务中积累的AI前沿技术，完美世界也在影视业务中持续释放技术溢出效应。今年10月，完美世界影视联合行业伙伴共同发起华语科幻AI影像联盟，未来将探索科幻IP与AI创制人才的双向创作生态。
在主业之外，完美世界还以财务投资的方式，借助专业机构间接参与前沿科技领域的成长机会。
根据公开披露的公告，今年从8月到10月，完美世界连续认购四只科技方向基金，基金方向均为新兴科技领域或前沿科技领域。单只基金出资额从5,000万元到5亿元不等，认购合计7.004亿元，资金全部来自自有资金，目前四只基金均已募集完毕。
完美世界在深交所投资者平台表示，公司目前经营稳健，经营性现金流充沛，货币资金储备充足。公司作为财务投资者参与基金投资，旨在提高闲置资金使用效率，获取长期财务回报；同时借助基金管理人的赛道资源和专业能力，对新兴产业方向开展前瞻布局。

在游戏新品迸发的下半年，Steam最吸引我的打折活动居然是烹饪游戏节。
现实生活中，我的做饭水平非常普通，经常被朋友评价为“每天做一些生命体征维系餐”。通常我做饭的步骤是：先下面条或者大米，再扔进去肉类，出锅前塞一把青菜——一个小电饭锅就能解决我所有吃饭问题。
但这不妨碍我对“烹饪”这件事有极高的兴趣，具体表现为我时常把烹饪比赛当作下饭配菜（可能单纯是因为自己做的太难吃了）、在B站和小红书收藏了几百个烹饪教程（小红书的AI给我整理收藏夹时指出，我点赞了很多懒人食谱）、在每一次烤非常简单的蛋挞时都拍精修图上传朋友圈……
听起来，我对于“烹饪”这件事可谓叶公好龙，仍旧处于一个空想阶段，但很多开放世界游戏内置的烹饪系统给了我一个幻想成真的机会，让我可以轻易制作（按几下屏幕）一些看起来很复杂的甚至很魔幻的料理。
而在一些mmo中，厨师也是经常会出现一种职业，这时做饭又成为了我游戏中的生活方式，比起刺客等刀尖舔血的职业，我更享受这种优哉游哉的感觉。游戏好友盯着悬赏榜接任务、快意恩仇时，我在收集材料、一键做菜、观察市场动向、在大赚特赚和亏得底朝天两个极端跳跃——用最近很流行的话来说，就是喜欢在游戏里做“日子人”。
随着对虚拟烹饪的喜爱逐步增加，我决定趁着史低购入好评如潮的烹饪模拟游戏《Chef Life: A Restaurant Simulator》（中文名：主厨人生），这时正好是Steam烹饪节，在活动页面逛了一圈后，我还顺便加购了新品《大厨的轮班》。
根据玩家们的建议，我还买了两个《主厨人生》的DLC，给自己未来的餐厅增添菜系，准备大肆烹饪一番。但一个周末过去了，我的《主厨人生》进度明显有些停滞。
也许是因为我意识到这款3D烹饪游戏似乎太过于还原现实，作为一个虚拟厨师，我需要操控角色移动，完成从拿取材料到结束洗碗的全步骤，容错率不低的初始关卡似乎快被我玩成了洗碗模拟器。现实中对烹饪极不擅长的氛围似乎蔓延到了游戏里，每一个步骤都会增添新的压力，让人颇有艰难学厨的感觉。
“我不是来体验这个的！”我想。
也有精通此游的朋友安慰我，说等手下有了“副厨”就熬出头了，从此可以享受轻松的厨房生活，不再需要老老实实地做菜。Steam评论区有一个幽默的评论也证实了这一点：
比起《主厨人生》，在《大厨的轮班》里做大厨则是更轻松写意的那一条世界线。
简单来说，这是一款打字烹饪游戏，玩家只要在键盘上打出对应的字词，就可以完成烤披萨、做咖啡、给客人上菜等多种行动。
虽然经常让我联想起小学时在计算机课上玩的《金山×××》，但加入烹饪和模拟经营元素后意外的很有趣，上手也很快。毕竟操作的逻辑非常简单，只要在看到词语出现的一瞬间争分夺秒地敲下键盘就好。
玩家当然也可以选择多国语言，给自己一种“我在学习外语”的错觉。可惜只是错觉，因为这些字词和动作本身没有关联，一连串的动作比如往披萨饼上撒料的过程也不会形成一个完整的句子——如果可以的话，我会给全世界正在外语学习中受苦的学生热烈推荐这款游戏。
简体中文的版本也还需要优化，人物对话翻译得有些生硬，有时还会突然冒出来一些英文词，非常破坏猛敲拼音的气氛，在字词长短的安排上也不如原始的英文版本来得顺手。
比如击毙偷偷溜进餐厅的老鼠（对于老鼠来说太残忍了所以我选择代入“黑手党”）时，在英文版本，玩家可以很简单地于混乱中瞬间敲下一两个字母，如“ya”、“o”，迅速地完成任务；而在中文版本里，有时设置的虽然也只是单字，但玩家有可能还需要敲上三到四下键盘。别小看这多出来的一下，也许我的客人等多了这一秒就耐心耗尽呢？
除了烹饪本身，游戏中也有一些很戏剧化的过场剧情，比如玩家操控的主角原本是一个盗贼、餐厅老板其实有隐藏身份、突然出现的美女有感情困扰等……像一部意大利黑帮题材肥皂剧，角色们留下一些令人震惊的对话，下一个关卡又开始了。
但当我敲键盘敲到冒烟，给客人做意面炸意式饺子时，会在心中产生一个疑问：
我真的下班了吗？
如果我已经下班了，而且今天还是周日，为什么我还在疯狂敲键盘啊？
news.title_cn: 触乐作者谈烹饪游戏：从《主厨人生》到《大厨的轮班》
news.what: 触乐作者讲述自己喜爱虚拟烹饪却现实中厨艺普通的经历，趁Steam烹饪游戏节购入《主厨人生》及DLC和打字烹饪游戏《大厨的轮班》，认为前者过于还原现实、操作压力大，后者上手快但中文本地化存在字词长度与翻译问题。

news.title: The Elder Scrolls 6 May Finally Have a Name Confirmation and It Makes Perfect Sense
news.summary_raw: Bethesda’s long-awaited RPG, The Elder Scrolls 6, reportedly has an official subtitle that connects directly to Hammerfell, earlier games, and a mystery fans seemingly solved months ago.

members.title: The Elder Scrolls 6 May Finally Have a Name Confirmation and It Makes Perfect Sense

news.body:
The Elder Scrolls 6 May Finally Have a Name Confirmation and It Makes Perfect Sense
Bethesda’s long-awaited RPG, The Elder Scrolls 6, reportedly has an official subtitle that connects directly to Hammerfell, earlier games, and a mystery fans seemingly solved months ago.
In case you missed it
The Elder Scrolls 6 Title
After more than eight years of referring to Bethesda’s next fantasy RPG simply as The Elder Scrolls VI, The Elder Scrolls 6, or even just TES 6, the long-awaited game may finally have its full name.
According to The Verge, sources familiar with Bethesda’s plans say the RPG is officially titled The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel. Bethesda could announce the name as soon as November, potentially aligning the reveal with the 15th anniversary of Skyrim on November 11. The Verge currently expects only a title announcement rather than a full gameplay presentation, even though it's reportedly "progressing well" so far.
The name should sound familiar to anyone who followed the clues Bethesda and Xbox dropped earlier this year. Xbox CEO Asha Sharma described watching a live playthrough of “The Elder Scrolls VI: ********” in August. Fans quickly noticed that “Sentinel” matched the eight concealed letters, while former Bethesda writer Michael Kirkbride responded affirmatively to the theory.
More importantly, Sentinel is not an arbitrary fantasy subtitle. It is a major Redguard kingdom and port city located in northwestern Hammerfell, overlooking the Iliac Bay. Bethesda’s original Daggerfall manual identifies Sentinel as one of Hammerfell’s kingdoms, and the city was one of the three principal powers surrounding the Iliac Bay in The Elder Scrolls II.
That makes the subtitle a natural fit for the game’s alleged Hammerfell setting. It also follows Bethesda’s established naming pattern: Daggerfall takes its name from a city, while Morrowind and Skyrim are named after provinces. Sentinel could indicate that the city and its surrounding kingdom will serve as the narrative center of a larger journey across Hammerfell and the surrounding areas.
The Verge reports that the game will explore the history of the Elder Scrolls themselves and reveal secrets surrounding the mysterious ancient artifacts. Apparently, Bethesda had discussed the setting as far back as Fallout 4’s development. The studio has since moved most of its team onto the project, with Todd Howard promising a return to Bethesda’s classic exploration-driven design. Although it seems like he'd still prefer everyone pretend the game hasn't been announced yet.
Bethesda has not officially confirmed the Sentinel name, but after years of silence following the 2018 teaser, that confirmation may finally be approaching, even if the game is allegedly still two or more years away.

news.title: How Hitman Devs Turned Jacksepticeye Into a “Violent Narcissist” in Newest Mission
news.summary_raw: IO Interactive explains how Jacksepticeye became Finn Colton, a narcissistic influencer whose content empire, buried trauma, and public facade shape Hitman’s new Elusive Target mission.

members.title: How Hitman Devs Turned Jacksepticeye Into a “Violent Narcissist” in Newest Mission

news.body:
How Hitman Devs Turned Jacksepticeye Into a “Violent Narcissist” in Newest Mission
IO Interactive explains how Jacksepticeye became Finn Colton, a narcissistic influencer whose content empire, buried trauma, and public facade shape Hitman’s new Elusive Target mission.
In case you missed it
Hitman Details
After spending years playing Hitman with his online community, YouTube Jacksepticeye has finally entered the World of Assassination—although not as himself. The creator, whose real name is Seán McLoughlin, portrays Finn Colton, better known as FinnVictus: a wealthy content creator, former children’s television star, exploitative employer, and suspected murderer operating from a constantly livestreamed compound in Hawke’s Bay.
The new mission, named The Host, is available as a free Elusive Target from October 29 through November 25, 2026, both for existing owners and through the game’s Free Demo. Agent 47 enters Colton’s compound as “thought leader” Tobias Rieper, ostensibly to appear on the Finn and Friends podcast, while avoiding the remote-controlled cameras recording almost every corner of the property.
Speaking with 80 Level, Senior Game Designer Eskil Møhl and Senior Level Designer Martin Skov Ansdal explained how an earlier Jacksepticeye cameo in 007 First Light developed into a much larger dramatic role. Rather than portraying the famously upbeat creator directly, IO Interactive used his natural charm and knowledge of online culture to create what Ansdal calls an amalgamation of “the absolute worst parts of the internet.”
Check out the game and the new mission while it's free until November 25.
IO Interactive
HITMAN has featured several celebrity Elusive Targets, but Jacksepticeye brings a very different public persona: energetic, joyful, kind, and deeply connected to online creator culture. What was the starting point for turning Seán McLoughlin into Finn Colton, also known as FinnVictus?
Eskil Møhl, Senior Game Designer at IO Interactive: Seán is indeed kind and energetic and was also game to play the worst version of online creators in this installment.
Martin Skov Ansdal, Senior Level Designer: We had a great experience working with Seán for a small cameo in 007 First Light. This inspired us to give him a much bigger dramatic role in HITMAN World of Assassination. Working with a YouTuber, we immediately thought of making his character an amalgamation of all the worst aspects of content creator culture. We went all in, on the knowledge that Seán would give this role a real authenticity based on his experience with that world.
Sean McLoughlin, aka Jacksepticeye
How do you design a target around a real person’s recognizable traits without simply making them a caricature? What details from Seán’s personality, content style, or creator background helped shape Finn Colton as an in-universe Hitman character?
Eskil Møhl: There’s some caricature in here and satirical commenting on certain internet phenomena; Seán is playing Finn here, not himself. His mannerisms and style as an over-the-top influencer couldn’t have been done by just anyone, so his background definitely helps make Finns’ far out persona somewhat believable.
Martin Skov Ansda: We look for their strengths as a performer and try to design a narrative that would utilize them. In Seán’s case, he is incredibly affable and has charm that cuts through to the audience on the other side of the screen. With Finn Colton we weaponize that effortless charm and turn it into a facade that gets gradually peeled away as the mission progresses. Finn Colton is a violent narcissist who performs charm effortlessly, and that makes for a great villain.
IO Interactive
Elusive Targets need to feel memorable very quickly, because players may only have one meaningful attempt to study and eliminate them. How did that structure influence the writing, mission setup, environmental storytelling, and level design around FinnVictus?
Eskil Møhl: The ET concept has developed over time, and especially with the celebrities, the missions have typically become more elaborate. The targets should shine, and as most are very good performers, you really want some movements with them where they are up front and center. They can now be played as special assignments, so players don’t become overly anxious about messing up as they want to toy around in the levels with the main attraction.
From a game design perspective, what makes a good Elusive Target in 2026? How do you balance novelty, player freedom, challenge, humor, and the pressure of a limited-time mission?
Eskil Møhl: The player freedom and systemics are there as base and foundation. Then a lot of the ideas for narrative and fantasy and what level the ET should take place on comes naturally from who is up. With Milla Jovovich we had a chance to pay homage to a franchise we love, and we had a big old mansion, a ruthless pharmaceutical company, and a contagious virus, so that’s how Lilith came to be. Snoop and Haven Island seemed like the right combination.
Who wouldn’t want to be at a Snoop party on an Island in the Indian Ocean? The well-known faces have brought something special and unique to the table each time. There is more often than not some underlying expectation of what flavor their mission should end up with. Humor and dark are then peppered in.
A lot of the humor and the dark bits come from the systemics themselves, but we also use the scripted dialog as a dial to turn up the lights or dim them when a moment calls for it.
Martin Skov Ansda: An Elusive Target has to simultaneously be a perfect introduction to Hitman as well as serve our hardcore fans. In some games, that duality might be hard to solve, but since Hitman is all about player freedom, we can design each mission like an iceberg – at the top we have an intuitive path which can be played without even having completed the tutorial, but then underneath we build layers of increasing complexity. The player can then choose to engage with the mission from whatever angle suits their level.
Since we now offer the elusive targets as Special assignments, the player can also replay the mission later and uncover the entire iceberg, this is the true strength of Hitman.
IO Interactive
What were the biggest creative challenges in designing a mission that reflects Seán’s personality while still fitting the darker, deadpan tone of HITMAN World of Assassination?
Eskil Møhl: As mentioned, Seán plays Finn in The Host. A very different persona than Seán himself. How much of themselves the celebrities bring into a level differs. Snoop is Dr. Cane, but it really is Snoop. Mads Mikkelsen was the established villain Le Chiffre he plays in Casino Royale. Wiz Khalifa brought his performer and martial arts persona and so on.
Finn is a nasty piece of work but of course, Seán isn’t at all, though his knowledge of that world and him being all aboard on the concept made that part of creating the level a joy.
Martin Skov Ansda: Agent 47 is a deadpan master of disguise and that conceit allows the character to fit into many different stories and environments. In some ways the game’s trademark dark comedy only becomes funnier the more outlandish the situation becomes. This allows World of Assassination to be incredibly tonally diverse.
This mission starts out as an overt parody of the content creator lifestyle – Seán’s performance is incredibly funny at first, but as the mission progresses and the mask peels away we see that Colton is a man with a pathological need for attention that comes from a place of trauma and we actually end up in a pretty dark place tonally
Can you walk us through the process of building Finn Colton as a character, from the initial concept and narrative role to likeness, wardrobe, animation, voice/performance considerations, behaviors, routines, and final implementation?
Martin Skov Ansda: We always play with our target’s public and a private persona and this duality is mirrored in the level design with public and private spaces.
Working with a YouTuber we immediately keyed in on the public persona as this high-energy content creator that completely dominates the private persona who is quite literally locked away in the basement.
IO Interactive
How did the team approach level design for this mission? What kinds of routes, disguises, opportunities, environmental clues, scripted moments, or player-driven possibilities were important to support the target’s identity?
Martin Skov Ansda: In every Hitman mission the player starts in public space and breaks into the characters private space as they progress towards eliminating the target.
This level centers around a single house which is essentially a representation of Finn’s personality. Upstairs is the zany kingdom of a high-energy content creator but downstairs he has hidden away all his trauma and malice.
The player must descend while constantly being filmed by Colton’s remote-controlled tripod cameras.
HITMAN missions often work because the comedy, violence, and systemic problem-solving all emerge naturally from the space. How do you design assassination opportunities that feel specific to this target without making the solution feel too obvious or too restrictive?
Eskil Møhl: Creating a moment with some poetic justice rarely falls flat. These can be heavily scripted but that gives us a chance to create good narrative and theater. Then the systemics are always there to take over when things go another way. I think they help balance each other in the ETs.
Martin Skov Ansda: It’s all about enticing the player to go down the most interesting paths instead of forcing them.
We present a target with a despicable personality flaw and then promise the opportunity for poetic justice. The player could always just pull out their gun and shoot Finn Colton in the face, but the promise of the perfect elimination, further exploring the level and the iceberg of dialogue and lore beckon the player to keep going.

news.title: Second Life Wants Its 23-Year-Old World To Be a Modern Game Platform
news.summary_raw: Linden Lab’s Anya Kanevsky explains how Luau, Visual Studio Code integration, live iteration, and an established creator economy could make Second Life more attractive to modern game developers.

members.title: Second Life Wants Its 23-Year-Old World To Be a Modern Game Platform

news.body:
Second Life Wants Its 23-Year-Old World To Be a Modern Game Platform
Linden Lab’s Anya Kanevsky explains how Luau, Visual Studio Code integration, live iteration, and an established creator economy could make Second Life more attractive to modern game developers.
More than two decades after its launch, Second Life is attempting to make its persistent virtual world considerably more approachable to contemporary game developers. With around 700,000 monthly active users, Linden Lab is introducing modern scripting through Lua in Second Life, a system closely related to Roblox’s high-performance Luau language, alongside Visual Studio Code integration and a workflow that allows creators to test changes directly inside its live multiplayer environment.
The update is not intended to replace the long-standing Linden Scripting Language or transform Second Life into a conventional game engine. Instead, Linden Lab wants to give creators a more familiar foundation for constructing and maintaining ambitious interconnected experiences.
In our interview, Linden Lab Senior Vice President of Product Anya Kanevsky discussed why Luau prevailed over alternatives such as C#, JavaScript, and WebAssembly; the challenges of safely running thousands of persistent scripts; and the opportunity for developers arriving from Roblox and other Lua-based environments.
Check out more details on the new platform tools here and read our full interview below.
ISM Moon Base Shackleton
Second Life has always been creator-driven, but full Lua scripting support feels like a major step toward positioning it more clearly as a modern game development platform. Why was Lua the right language to bring into Second Life now?
Linden Lab Senior Vice President of Product, Anya Kanevsky: Lua gives us an opportunity to modernize scripting in Second Life while preserving what makes Second Life unique as a creator platform. Interestingly, we didn’t start this project by saying, “We need Lua.” We evaluated a wide range of options (including C#, JavaScript and WebAssembly) against some very unusual technical requirements that come with Second Life. Scripts need to run securely alongside thousands of other scripts, pause and resume, preserve their state, and even move between servers as objects travel across regions or into inventory. Luau ultimately provided the best fit across those requirements.
The added benefit is that Lua is already familiar to a very large community of game developers. So we ended up with a technical solution that improves the experience for our existing creators while also lowering the barrier for developers who have never built in Second Life before.
Lua and Luau are already familiar to many developers across games, including Roblox creators. How much of this update is aimed at making Second Life more approachable for developers coming from Roblox or other Lua-based environments?
Anya Kanevsky: It’s really two things at once. First, Lua dramatically lowers the learning curve for developers coming from other environments. Someone who already understands Lua or Luau can arrive in Second Life and right away they can start experimenting. That certainly includes Roblox developers, but it’s broader than Roblox. Lua has a long history across game development, so there’s a substantial developer community for whom the language and programming concepts will already feel familiar.
Secondly, this is an investment in the creators who are already building in Second Life. We want to give them a more modern, efficient scripting environment while continuing to support our own Linden Scripting Language (LSL), and while Lua offers more functionality, Lua and LSL scripts can coexist - even within the same object. In our earliest tests with creators, we heard positive feedback about the increased memory limits and the ability to now do more overall with Lua in Second Life using fewer scripts compared to LSL.
Most importantly both of these things are actually an investment in the overall diversity of experiences of all residents in Second Life. By giving creators more powerful tools, we make sure that everyone has more fun.
For developers who have never built in Second Life before, what kinds of interactive experiences or games does Lua unlock that were harder to create with the existing toolset?
Anya Kanevsky: What Lua changes is how developers can build and evolve them. It provides modern language features and programming patterns that make larger systems easier to structure, maintain and extend. Things like tables, dynamic event handling, coroutines, JSON support and optional type annotations give developers tools that are much more familiar from contemporary development environments.
The important distinction is that Lua doesn’t suddenly make games possible in Second Life. Residents have been creating remarkably sophisticated games and interactive experiences with LSL for many years.
So we think the opportunity is both about saying, “Here is a game you could never build before,” and even more about making ambitious projects easier to develop and maintain - and making Second Life much more approachable to developers who already know modern scripting languages.
The pitch here is not just that developers can script content, but that they can launch and update scripts live in-world. How does that workflow change the way creators can prototype, test, and iterate on game systems?
Anya Kanevsky: Live iteration has actually been part of Second Life development for a long time. Creators have always been able to modify scripts and immediately see the results in-world, and collaborative building has been a cornerstone of Second Life creativity as a result. Lua and the development workflow we’re rolling out is making it easy for the creativity to flow.
Our integration with Visual Studio Code lets developers work in a professional development environment while connecting that work directly to objects in Second Life. That means creators can benefit from familiar development tools for navigating and managing code and working with objects and linksets, while still seeing their changes reflected in the live virtual world. Our recent work on the client specifically improves communication between Second Life and the VS Code extension, including live exploration of objects and linksets.
That creates a very fast creative loop: write, test in the actual multiplayer environment, adjust, and test again.
MIRROMERE
Second Life has a smaller user base than platforms like Roblox, but the creator monetization numbers are compelling. How do you explain the economic opportunity for developers who are used to building on much larger platforms?
Anya Kanevsky: Scale is only one side of the creator opportunity. The other is economics: if you build something people value, how much of that value can you actually capture?
Second Life has had a functioning user-to-user economy for more than two decades. Creators can sell directly to residents in-world and through the Second Life Marketplace. Linden Dollars can be exchanged for real-world currency, and creators retain control over their intellectual property. Our current creator economics are structured around creators keeping approximately 85% of their sales revenue before applicable cash-out fees (which compares quite favorably to what Roblox pays).
So our pitch isn't that Second Life has a larger audience than Roblox - it doesn't. Second Life offers a mature audience with an established culture of spending money on user-created content and an economic model designed to let creators retain a substantial share of the value they create. We think Second Life offers an opportunity for established creators to extend their reach and audiences from other platforms to augment their existing income streams and also to expand their creative reach in ways not possible on other more restrictive platforms. In particular, we think there is a new opportunity for creators to bring over their established followers into an entirely new space to not only extend their income, but also their creative reach with deeper and more engaging experiences.
How healthy is the user base? How many people are building in SL each month and how many are there just to play? Are builders actually making money from this platform?
Anya Kanevsky: Second Life is unusual because the line between “player” and “creator” is much less rigid than it is on many game platforms. Someone might socialize or roleplay one day, customize an avatar or home the next, and eventually begin making and selling their own content while still remaining part of a tight-knit community inworld. As far as numbers go, we have had a fairly stable number of highly-engaged Monthly Active Users (MAUs) for several years.
We average just under 700,000 monthly active users consistently with just over 11% of users actively scripting and creating content either for fun or profit. So, yes, creators make real money. Second Life has supported a functioning creator economy for more than two decades, with Linden Dollars convertible to real-world currency. So far this year, we have had over 13,000 unique creators cashing out with real money from their creations. In this difficult economy, Second Life can offer a vital "side hustle" that is both profitable and creatively fulfilling.
LeLoo's World - Dancing Leaves
What kinds of lessons do you think Roblox developers could bring into Second Life, and where do you think they would need to think differently because of Second Life’s culture, audience, economy, and virtual-world structure?
Anya Kanevsky: There is a lot of knowledge that transfers directly: designing compelling gameplay loops, progression systems, multiplayer interactions, live content updates and experiences that encourage people to return.
Where Second Life becomes very different is that you're not necessarily building an isolated game session. You're building inside a persistent virtual world with its own communities

news.title: Newly merged Skydance mandates staff return to office five days a week, offers Voluntary Buyout Program
news.summary_raw: The newly merged Skydance Corporation has mandated employees return to the office for five days a week and is offering a Voluntary Buyout Program (VBO).

members.title: Newly merged Skydance mandates staff return to office five days a week, offers Voluntary Buyout Program

news.body:
Newly merged Skydance mandates staff return to office five days a week, offers Voluntary Buyout Program
Skydance CEO David Ellison and co-CEO Ynon Kreiz say RTO policy "is in the best interest" of employees
The newly merged Skydance Corporation has mandated employees return to the office for five days a week and is offering a Voluntary Buyout Program (VBO).
Earlier this month, Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery completed a $111 billion merger and now operate under Skydance. Paramount Games Studio and WB Games were combined into a single unit managed by Tony Driscoll.
In an email to staff seen by Vertical Slice, Skydance CEO David Ellison and co-CEO Ynon Kreiz said they believe a five-day in-office policy across the entire company "is in the best interest" of its staff.
"We've seen the benefits firsthand at Paramount, and we want every part of Skydance to share in them," the email read. "The best ideas come from people in the same room, sharing perspectives, challenging one another and solving problems. Being together isn't just about showing up. It's about inspiring one another, learning and coaching, forming friendships and having access to the casual conversations that spark something great."
Vertical Slice reports that the return-to-office policy will be "rolled out in phases based on location," and that employees will receive "ample notice" before any changes are made.
It also stated that Skydance "may revisit remote roles" as the process takes place, and that those in fully remote positions will not be subject "to immediate change".
Alongside this announcement, Skydance outlined the terms of its VBO.
"As we bring our teams together, we recognise that not everyone will see their future here and we respect that," the email read. "To give eligible employees the option to move on in a way that works for them, we are introducing a Voluntary Buyout Program."
Earlier this week, Microsoft offered voluntary exit to up to 60,000 employees, including Xbox staff.
In the initial merger announcement, Skydance CEO David Ellison stated that the merger will require the company to make "difficult decisions," including "changes and impacts."
"Bringing together two companies of this size and complexity will require difficult decisions. There will be changes, and there will be impacts. I'm not going to pretend otherwise," said Ellison.

news.title: "We are very eager to learn from the real veterans" – How Tencent's TiMi Studio Group collaborated with Capcom on Monster Hunter Outlanders
news.summary_raw: Today marks the release of Monster Hunter Outlanders, a mobile version of Capcom's long-running franchise that has been created by Tencent's TiMi Studio Group.

members.title: "We are very eager to learn from the real veterans" – How Tencent's TiMi Studio Group collaborated with Capcom on Monster Hunter Outlanders

news.body:
"We are very eager to learn from the real veterans" – How Tencent's TiMi Studio Group collaborated with Capcom on Monster Hunter Outlanders
The development director for the new mobile title, which launches today, explains TiMi's working relationship with Capcom and what's changed in the transition to mobile devices
Today marks the release of Monster Hunter Outlanders, a mobile version of Capcom's long-running franchise that has been created by Tencent's TiMi Studio Group.
Previously, Niantic brought Monster Hunter to mobile with Monster Hunter Now, but whereas that title was an AR game along similar lines to Niantic's Pokémon Go, TiMi's Monster Hunter Outlanders aims to distil the "full-fat" Monster Hunter experience onto a mobile device. (Interestingly, TiMi has competition from Capcom itself on this front, following the recent surprise announcement that the console game Monster Hunter Rise has now been brought to mobile via Netflix.)
GamesIndustry.biz spoke with Bryan Li, the development director for Monster Hunter Outlanders, about the changes needed to make Capcom's game sing on mobile devices, as well as TiMi's working relationship with Capcom.
What problems did you have trying to translate the game to mobile?
At the very beginning of the project, the team spent a lot of time identifying what could be the sweet balance between maintaining a very truthful and authentic Monster Hunter experience, and yet at the same time make sure it feels very visceral and very native to mobile devices.
Luckily, the majority of my team members have been long-term, loyal fans of the entire franchise, so they know every single element of the entire brand. A lot of those great symbolic elements are carried on and preserved in Monster Hunter Outlanders: those familiar monsters, those familiar weapons, the touch and feel, the impact.
But at the same time, only replicating a similar kind of Monster Hunter experience was not going to be good enough, so the team took a lot of effort in fine tuning, especially with the controls. This is why the team came up with two solutions, with the Classic Mode more favoured towards relatively experienced mobile action game users, while the simplified Adventure Mode is tailored towards players who are less experienced with the franchise.
Besides the control tweaks and adaptation to mobile devices, the team also took a lot of extra miles thinking about what additional innovation we can bring to the game, hence you will see there's a full new main storyline. On top of that, having an interesting world-touring experience is not only about how big your map is, it's really about having enough fun elements to populate the world.
It seems you've really expanded on that last point, adding more activities that you wouldn't normally get in the main game.
Exactly. Our level designers spend hours fine-tuning those golden paths for the player to make sure that whenever they have a major quest objective, they're able to use a very fluent way to get there, while at the same time there are also interesting and wonderful opportunities alongside those golden paths. People can always expect something new, something rewarding along their way. On top of that, the team spent a lot of effort on the crafting system, and although we don't have a riding system, there are different gadgets like zip lines and ballistas to enrich the navigation experience.
With mobile, playtimes tend to be much shorter than on PC and console, how have you accommodated that?
Shortening the gameplay session duration is the natural choice: the difficulty is finding the sweet spot. The team did a lot of iteration on that. We are good at proposing different kinds of hypotheses, but we might not be able to hit the spot on the first try, and that's why we always, always conduct several rounds of playtest sessions and live test sessions. We invite the players to evaluate our hypothesis together with us.
Did you take any lessons from Niantic's mobile title Monster Hunter Now?
Well, to be honest with you, we don't really have too much direct communication with Niantic, but since we are all part of the Capcom Monster Hunter ecosystem, we do have a lot of publishing-related knowledge sharings about what people are actually expecting from Monster Hunter mobile games, and what people don't like that much in terms of making a mobile version of Monster Hunter. So we exchanged those key know-hows and best practices with our counterpart from the Capcom side.
How closely do you work with Capcom, and what does that relationship look like?
Although our major areas of expertise are slightly different from each other, some of the guiding principles and philosophies are quite common in nature. For example, both of our companies really value player feedback, so it's very natural for us to have this kind of conversation with our counterpart from Capcom. We carefully listen to the players' feedback and take on their valuable input.
On Capcom's side, they know the franchise in and out, and we are lucky to have the opportunity to learn from them how you define your core combat mechanism, and how to make a believable creature for the Monster Hunter universe. On Tencent's side, we have a relatively richer experience of long-term free-to-play live service items, so we share with our counterparts not only what we are doing and the planning for the initial release, but also our approach in terms of the longer-term post-launch roadmap.
In a way, Capcom has entrusted you with its crown jewels.
Exactly. It's a blessing for us to be able to work on the project.
How did you earn that trust? How did you convince them to let you work on Monster Hunter?
Capcom is a company that welcomes a lot of different new and innovative ideas to further enrich the overall ecosystem of the brand, while on the Tencent side, we are very eager to learn from the real veterans of the industry. As I mentioned, a lot of our team members are diehard fans of the franchise, and a small team from our side took the opportunity to pitch in front of Capcom, which triggered the collaboration.
In terms of building up the relationship, it's really about two things. First, we speak and collaborate in very professional terms. On top of that, it's really about taking time to build up your relationship. You won't really have the honeymoon sessions at the very beginning. It takes time. You basically accumulate the success stories one by one. And at the moment, we are able to have this kind of strategic relationship where we are able to openly discuss any kind of topic and really trust each other.
What does the process look like? Are you left completely to your own devices, or is Capcom giving you direction every step of the way? Or is it somewhere in between?
We have a lot of regular conversations with our counterparts from the Capcom side. We exchange different kinds of design ideas, different kinds of intentions to validate those ideas, and make sure that we are able to reach a mutual agreement. They are the IP owners, so whatever kind of innovative idea we have, it is really a way of respect to make sure that we actually pitch the idea in front of them. So far, I would say the Capcom side is very collaborative and supportive, and they encourage us to bring a lot of different, innovative ideas.
It sounds like you're proposing the ideas rather than Capcom saying 'You should do this'.
Exactly.
Obviously the mainstream games are premium titles, so I wonder what kind of monetisation system you're using for Monster Hunter Outlanders?
That's the billion-dollar question, and I'm pretty sure that a lot of players will be eager to know that. Being a free-to-play mobile game, without spending a single penny, people will be able to enjoy all the storylines, all the core game modules, and all the key function systems without any kind of problems.
Our monetisation will only be captured in three major categories. The first one is basically the avenue for you to acquire new adventures, but it doesn't mean those new adventures will be more powerful than other adventures. It's just merely offering additional hunting styles for players to really tailor their hunting experience as they wish.
Secondly, we offer a vast amount of customization and vanity item opportunities. Once again, we have zero intention to sell power through those customizations, it's merely an avenue for the players to show their own self-expression. And thirdly, it's really about time saving and convenience, because we want the players to have the freedom to choose how they want to invest their time and enjoy the game as they wish.
This interview has been edited for length and clarity.

members.title: "I wish I had the formula" – 2Awesome Studio on navigating indie development while creating Altered Alma, its biggest project to date

news.body:
"I wish I had the formula" – 2Awesome Studio on navigating indie development while creating Altered Alma, its biggest project to date
Co-founder Alexander Santiago discusses running a studio in a market of "smaller teams delivering bigger successes"
Last week, indie publisher Critical Reflex hosted its annual showcase, featuring a host of hard-to-define titles including Altered Alma, a cyberpunk-infused Metroidvania from Barcelona-based 2Awesome Studio.
2Awesome is finalizing its largest title to date, which raised over €260,000 from more than 5,100 Kickstarter backers. Launched in 2024, the campaign initially aimed for €40,000.
As Altered Alma nears completion, 2Awesome co-founder Alexander Santiago tells GamesIndustry.biz that the team is optimistic about the game's launch.
"Wishlist numbers are looking really good; we featured in Steam Next Fest and had a really good reception. We're always going to different events. We were in the Indie Arena at Gamescom, which is a seal of quality because the games are curated. When you get in that, your game has something. We're going in the right direction."
Development on Altered Alma started in 2023, at a time when the industry had "big projects and big budgets," says Santiago. "Altered Alma was a challenging and ambitious project for us. It's the biggest game we've done, biggest team, biggest scope, biggest everything. It's an open-world Metroidvania, so it requires effort."
Drawing on this experience, Santiago is confident 2Awesome will streamline development for its next project. The team plans to continue the Altered Alma franchise with a more focused scope.
"Looking at the overall industry for newer IPs and projects, it's focused on smaller budgets and focused games – doing one or two things really well. I think that's where we are right now. There are always bigger budgets, and hopefully we'll have a sequel in the oven at some point."
Since its founding in 2014, 2Awesome Studio has relied on multiple funding sources. "It's all been Kickstarter, government funding, loans, [and support from] publishers," he notes.
Before Altered Alma, the team ran two successful Kickstarter campaigns. Their first title, Dimension Dive, raised €36,996 from over 1,000 backers and launched in 2017. AK-xolotl, funded in 2022 with €132,807 from a €15,000 goal and over 2,500 backers, launched in 2023.
The developer also offers outsourcing as an additional income stream. "It's not our core business, but we need to keep the lights on, so we provide services for others. There is no one solution that fits all."
Santiago notes that outsourcing and co-development are also challenging markets to enter. "It was a natural evolution for us with our first game, deciding to do the ports in-house. It was a technical decision to gain experience; not because of a long-term plan, just because we wanted the know-how."
" We're trying to gauge the market now and, with our knowledge, fit into it"
"After that, we worked with Focus Home Interactive to port Othercide to Switch," he continues. "Then we got a reputation, and it spread by word of mouth. That's what works best for us, like, 'Ah, yeah, these guys deliver what they promise, say, 99% of the time, all the time.' That's quite unique in the industry."
2Awesome Studio appears to have developed a successful approach to indie development, balancing multiple income streams and a clear franchise roadmap.
However, Santiago says there is no universal formula for running an indie studio. "I wish I had the formula," Santiago laughs. "We don't have it. We are planning for the next two or three years, which hopefully includes the sequel for Altered Alma."
"As I said, we are a smaller studio. We have some changes in the plan, things we couldn't do in the first game that we want to include in the sequel. We're trying to gauge the market now and, with our knowledge, fit into it; especially as more smaller teams deliver bigger successes. There are two sides – smaller and bigger projects. We're trying to fit in both."

members.title: 长大以后，我们为什么还想要一场“冒险”：机核专访《禁闭求生2》执行制作人 Marcus

features.body:
《禁闭求生2》是一款由黑曜石娱乐开发的生存冒险游戏，玩家将缩小至昆虫般的尺寸，在危机四伏的后院中探索未知、收集资源、建造基地，并与伙伴携手展开一场充满惊喜与挑战的微观大冒险。
而在刚刚举办的“北京核聚变 2026”现场，我采访到了本作的执行制作人 Marcus Edward Morgan。对他来说，这趟中国之行不仅是一次普通的线下活动，也是一个难得的机会：能够亲眼看看远在大洋彼岸的玩家，究竟是怎样看待这款游戏的。
聊起对核聚变的印象时，Marcus 显得相当兴奋。他告诉我，自己以前参加过不少游戏展会，包括科隆游戏展，以及已经停办的 E3。不过，即便有过这么多经历，这次的“核聚变”依然给他留下了很深的印象。
“说实话，这是我最喜欢的展会之一。”他解释说，自己原本没有想到，现场会有这么多玩家前来体验游戏。能够看到中国玩家玩得开心，他自己也感到非常高兴。
其实这份“中国玩家的热情”并非没有来由 —— 今年 10 月，《禁闭求生2》推出了秋季更新“Rot and Ruin”，带来了全新区域“Woodpile”、玩家期待已久的蜈蚣 Boss，以及基地涂装和马铃薯甲虫虫骑等新内容。对于已经在后院里生存了很长时间的玩家来说，这些新东西不仅意味着又有地方可以探索，也意味着熟悉的生存、战斗与建造玩法还在不断发生变化。
当然，更新内容越多，玩家想问的问题也就越多：接下来还会有什么新区域？开发团队会怎样处理玩家的反馈？那些让人头皮发麻的大型昆虫，又会带来怎样的挑战？
带着这些问题，我和 Marcus 聊了起来。采访刚开始，我就先提到了自己的事情。我告诉他，我经常和妻子一起玩《禁闭求生2》，而她尤其喜欢这款游戏。听到这里，Marcus 显得相当高兴，笑着说：“那你可得带点儿我们这的小周边回去给她。”
这倒是一个不错的开场。毕竟，对于《禁闭求生2》这样的游戏来说，和朋友、家人一起组队探索世界，本来就是游戏中最有乐趣的一部分。
但很快，我就发现，Marcus 本人也是个相当有趣的采访对象。
聊到游戏未来的更新计划时，我问 Marcus，团队接下来是会优先扩展地图、加入新生物和装备，还是继续丰富生存、建造与探索系统？
他告诉我，《禁闭求生2》的更新大致分成两种类型。一种更偏向内容扩展，例如此前的“Into the Abyss”更新，就把重点放在水下区域和新的探索体验上；另一种则更侧重功能与系统，比如刚刚推出的“Rot and Ruin”，基地涂装就是其中一项新功能。
这两种更新会交替进行。也就是说，玩家既能期待新区域和新冒险，也不用担心那些已经熟悉的玩法就此停滞。
说到这里，Marcus 开始谨慎起来。“我得想清楚哪些东西已经可以说，哪些还不能说。”他笑着解释，“你们可能不知道，我在和社区交流的时候有个外号，叫“Mr. Drips”。一方面是因为我平时穿衣服比较有趣，另一方面就是因为我总是忍不住透露一些消息。 ”
其实今天公关经理 Shyla Lane Schofie 一起出现在采访现场，并且这时候就在我们俩的旁边，某种程度上就是为了防止他讲得太多。看来，采访一位执行制作人，有时候还得顺便考验一下公关经理的反应速度。
不过，尽管 Marcus 一再提醒自己不要说漏嘴，他还是透露了一点值得期待的消息：接下来的冬季更新会带来新的探索内容，而地图上还有一片尚待玩家探索的区域。熟悉现有地图的玩家，或许已经能够猜到它的位置。
更有意思的是，这片区域与游戏开场发生爆炸的地方有关。玩家将有机会前往那里，看看爆炸之后究竟发生了什么。至于具体会遇到什么，Marcus 暂时没有给我透露出来。毕竟，“Mr. Drips”已经够容易说漏嘴了，总不能让他在采访结束前就把底牌全交出来。
除了新区域，他还提到了一个自己很期待玩家体验的方向：游戏中的原始科学，也就是玩家熟悉的紫色科技点数 —— “如果原始科学不断变多，那么它会如何影响玩家，又会如何影响周围的世界呢？”我这样问他。
这个问题听起来有些抽象，但 Marcus 认为，这恰恰是一个《禁闭求生 2》继续探索的方向。对于一款已经建立起相当完整的生存世界的游戏来说，新内容不一定只是增加几种昆虫、几件装备，也可以从玩家已经熟悉的系统入手，来继续深入挖掘它们还能带来什么变化。
当然，如果问 Marcus 本人最喜欢哪种更新的方向，答案可能就没那么抽象了。
“我喜欢有难度的游戏。”他说。随着《禁闭求生2》逐渐接近正式版，他希望玩家能够运用此前积累的经验，面对越来越有挑战性的敌人和遭遇。对他来说，这次更新里的蜈蚣 Boss，就是一个很好的例子。
蜈蚣的加入并不是开发团队突然冒出来的想法。Marcus 告诉我，这个 Boss 本身就来自社区的期待，团队在规划后续内容时，会专门整理玩家提出的建议，并把它们纳入开发计划。
“我们一直在听取社区的意见。”他说。开发团队每周都会和社区经理坐下来，整理玩家的反馈，并讨论哪些问题应该优先处理。不过，听取意见并不意味着玩家提出什么，团队就一定照着做什么。
Marcus 举了一个很值得注意的例子：有时候，玩家会指出某个功能存在问题，同时也会提出自己认为可行的解决方案。但开发者需要进一步弄清楚，问题究竟出在哪里。因为玩家提出的解决办法未必是最合适的选择，只有找到问题背后的原因，才有可能从根本上改善体验。
团队也希望尽可能坦诚地向玩家解释自己的决定。如果某项建议会被采纳，他们会尽量说明将如何调整；如果暂时无法实现，也希望玩家能够理解背后的原因。
对 Marcus 来说，这种持续的交流，也是开发《禁闭求生2》很有意思的一部分。等到游戏正式推出 1.0 版本时，他希望玩家能够感受到，自己确实参与进了这款游戏的成长之中。
不过，社区的呼声只是原因之一。开发团队在设计新区域时，也会思考哪些昆虫适合成为 Boss，哪些生物能够给玩家带来既恐怖又有趣的体验。蜈蚣本身就具备这样的特点：它行动迅速，身体细长，多足移动时又很容易让人产生不适感。
更重要的是，它和这次更新的“Woodpile”区域也很契合。这个区域里有白蚁等生物，而蜈蚣的出现，也与它们所处的环境联系在一起。团队希望在自己的幻想和现实生物的习性之间找到平衡，让玩家觉得这个世界既充满想象力，又有一些可以理解的逻辑。
至于如何把蜈蚣的生物特征转化成战斗机制，Marcus 的回答同样很直接：先观察它在现实中是怎样行动的 —— 他说：“对蜈蚣而言，它最让人害怕的地方之一，就是移动速度非常快。它会迅速地爬行、转向，让你很难判断它下一步会做什么。”而它的外壳又很坚硬，所以一味攻击身体并不是最有效的办法。玩家需要抓住机会，攻击它相对脆弱的腹部。
换句话说，这场战斗并不只是把一只巨大的蜈蚣放进游戏，再给它安排一条很长的血条。开发团队希望玩家能够从它的外形和习性中，逐渐摸索出应对方式。
当然，面对一只体型远超自己的蜈蚣，光是保持冷静可能就已经是一项挑战了。我也问了 Marcus 一个更实际的问题：随着玩家越来越熟悉游戏，团队该怎样在战斗难度和机制复杂度之间找到平衡？
他的回答是，开发团队会根据不同阶段的玩家群体，调整游戏的体验。
在抢先体验阶段，进入游戏的玩家往往更熟悉游戏的玩法，也更愿意挑战有难度的内容，因此团队可以尝试加入更复杂的机制和更强大的 Boss。但当大型更新吸引新玩家加入时，开发团队就会重新审视整个新手的引导部分。
例如此前的水下更新“Into the Abyss”，由于有新的玩家群体加入，团队就会考虑怎样让初次进入游戏的人更容易上手。调整范围不仅包括引导，也可能涉及生物的位置和玩家能够选择的探索路线。
这意味着，开发团队考虑的并不只是某场 Boss 战是否足够刺激，还要考虑玩家是在什么阶段遇到它，以及他们此前积累了多少经验。而对于一款仍在持续扩展内容的生存游戏来说，挑战可以越来越高，但玩家也需要有一个逐渐适应这个世界的台阶才对。
当然，《禁闭求生2》并不是一款只聚焦于战斗的游戏。
对不少玩家来说，收集材料、搭建基地，再把自己的小窝一点点扩展起来，同样是游戏中很重要的乐趣。这次“Rot and Ruin”更新加入的基地涂装功能，就是一个很好的例子。
我问 Marcus，既然玩家已经能够建造各种各样的建筑，为什么直到这次更新，团队才加入给基地上色的功能？
他的解释是，开发团队希望先提供足够丰富的建造部件，再逐渐扩展玩家能够进行的个性化调整。颜色并不只是一个简单的装饰选项：如果处理得不好，一些原本具有自然质感的材料，涂上颜色之后反而可能显得奇怪。
因此，团队也对能够上色的物件做了一些限制。墙壁、地板、天花板等建筑部件可以使用涂装工具进行调整，但并不是所有装置和功能性物件都能上色。
当然这并不意味着这些限制以后就永远都不会改变。“等玩家真正开始使用这个功能之后，我们肯定还会根据他们的反馈继续调整的。”Marcus 表示。
我觉得这倒是一个很有意思的开发思路。对于建造玩法来说，玩家的需求往往并不是一开始就能全部预料到的。有些人可能只是想让基地看起来更漂亮，也有人会把不同颜色当成一种标记方式，甚至围绕它发展出自己的建造风格。功能上线之后，玩家究竟能玩出多少花样，反过来也会成为开发团队继续完善系统的参考。
在这次更新中，玩家还获得了一种新的出行方式：马铃薯甲虫虫骑。我问 Macus，“它和之前的瓢虫虫骑有什么区别？ ”
“它拥有更坚固的防御，也更加耐打。与此同时，它背上的炮能够提供更多应对战斗的选择。《禁闭求生2》里有不同的装备与成长层级，随着玩家不断推进游戏，他们也需要更强大的工具来面对新的挑战。马铃薯甲虫虫骑就是在这样的基础上设计的。
它不仅更强，也能让玩家用不同的方式去应对新的敌人。这套设计和游戏里的成长节奏联系得很紧密：玩家探索得越深入，就越需要新的工具来应对更危险的环境。虫骑也就不只是一个方便赶路的交通工具，而是成为了玩家战斗和探索方式的一部分。
从蜈蚣 Boss 到基地涂装，再到新的虫骑，这次更新涉及的内容看起来各不相同，但它们最终都指向了同一个方向：继续拓展玩家在这个世界里的“能做的事情”。对《禁闭求生2》本身而言，追加的这些玩法，更像是一颗枝繁叶茂的大树，在不断对外生长后所结下的果实。
谈到玩家反馈时，我还问 Marcus，有没有什么反应让开发团队感到意外，或者让他们意识到，某种设计方向可能比预想中更受欢迎。他想了一会儿，提到了一个和战斗有关的变化：在《禁闭求生2》中，玩家终于有机会与一个人类敌人交手。
这个神秘人会在游戏中跟踪玩家。与第一代主要面对昆虫的战斗相比，这样的对手显然带来了不同的感觉——玩家面对的不再只是一只具有特殊习性的生物，而是一个拥有和自己相近能力的对手。
Marcus 说，团队此前也有些忐忑，不知道玩家会如何接受这样的设计。但结果让他们相当高兴，玩家对这部分内容的反应很好。
“我们希望在游戏中加入更多不同类型的遭遇。”他说。“我们希望继续拓展玩家在这个世界里能够经历的事情，而不只是不断增加新的昆虫。 ”
我觉得这也是《禁闭求生2》后续内容值得关注的地方。随着玩家逐渐熟悉昆虫的习性、装备的搭配和战斗的节奏，如果所有挑战都只是更大的虫子、更厚的护甲和更高的伤害，游戏的体验难免会变得重复。新的敌人类型，则有机会改变玩家对危险的判断方式。
当然，具体还会加入什么样的遭遇，Marcus 并没有在采访中透露更多。不过，结合他此前提到的内容更新方向，团队显然不希望玩家在熟悉了现有玩法之后，就再也遇不到新的惊喜。
在 Marcus 看来，《禁闭求生》系列最吸引人的地方，是一种近乎童真的幻想。
我们平时走在户外，看到草地、石头、昆虫，往往不会觉得有什么特别。但如果有一天，我们突然缩小到蚂蚁那么大，原本熟悉的环境就会变成完全不同的世界。草叶成了高耸的树林，一些不起眼的小东西也可能成为巨大的障碍，而一次普通的探索，则可能变成一场冒险。
“你可以想象，如果自己变得很小，世界会是什么样子。”Marcus 说。
他希望《禁闭求生2》能够尽可能地让玩家沉浸在这种体验里。未来加入更多生物、更多区域，以及更多可以探索的幻想，都是为了让这个世界变得更加丰富。
他举了一个很形象的例子：对于一个缩小到蚂蚁大小的人来说，爬上一支冰淇淋甜筒，可能就和攀登珠穆朗玛峰一样壮观。
这也是他认为游戏最特别的地方——当我们的视角发生变化，原本平凡的事物也会变得不可思议。
不过，Marcus 随后又补充了另一个他很看重的部分：和朋友一起玩游戏的感觉。
他希望玩家在《禁闭求生2》中获得的，不只是探索一个奇妙世界的乐趣，还有一种仿佛重新回到童年的体验。大家聚在一起，发挥自己的想象力，一起面对冒险中的麻烦，也一起分享那些意料之外的发现。
这种连接既存在于玩家和玩家之间，也存在于玩家与开发团队之间。玩家的反馈会影响游戏的发展，而共同游玩的经历，则可能成为玩家自己珍藏的回忆。
聊到这里，Marcus 突然反问我，“你觉得自己最喜欢《禁闭求生 2》的原因是什么呢？”
我告诉他，虽然《禁闭求生2》的设定很容易让人联想到青少年时期的冒险幻想，但这款游戏意外地吸引了我这样一个即将年满 40 岁的玩家。
小时候，我们并没有现在这么多电子娱乐设备。和朋友在一起时，很多乐趣都来自一些很简单的事情：玩泥巴、堆沙子，或者拿着玩具，把眼前的环境想象成一个更大的世界。长大之后，这些经历似乎逐渐离我远去了，但在《禁闭求生2》中，我却又找到了那种感觉。
Marcus 听完后笑的很开心，他说在这一点上，大家都是一样的。他认为，游戏当然可以吸引年轻玩家，但同样也应该适合成年人、父母和家庭。对于年轻玩家来说，它可以是一场全新的幻想；对于已经长大的人来说，它也可以让人重新找回过去的想象力。
我告诉 Marcus，平时工作比较忙的时候，我和妻子有时很少有机会像过去那样交流。但自从我们一起玩《禁闭求生2》之后，反而找回了不少儿时的记忆，也重新获得了许多共同的话题。这是我在开始玩这款游戏时，完全没有预料到的收获。
听到这里，Marcus 表示他很高兴能听到一些他意料之外的好事情，然后他也好奇地问了我这样一个问题：明明游戏里的环境并不是中国的后院，为什么它依然能够带来这样的怀旧感？
小时候玩玩具时，我们经常会幻想自己就是玩具里的角色，在窗台上、房间里展开一场大冒险。就像《玩具总动员》那样，当我们换成玩具的视角去观察世界，原本熟悉的环境也会变得陌生而奇妙。
Marcus 听完后表示，这正是他希望游戏能够传达的感受：虽然不同国家和地区的生活环境各不相同，但想象自己变得很小、从另一个视角重新认识世界，却是一种很容易引起共鸣的幻想。
聊到不同文化之间的共鸣时，我也顺势问了 Marcus 一个问题：《禁闭求生》系列的背景很容易让人联想到美国的后院文化，但中国玩家的生活环境与美国并不完全相同。团队是否担心过，这种文化差异会影响中国玩家的体验？
Marcus 承认，这确实是团队会思考的问题，而且并不只发生在中国 —— 不同地区的生活环境和常见生物各不相同，例如英国人可能更习惯把自家户外空间称为花园，而不是美国语境中的后院。
但他认为，《禁闭求生2》的核心体验并不局限于某一个国家的生活方式。无论玩家生活在哪里，大多数人都见过昆虫，也都可能想象过，如果自己突然变得很小，周围的世界会发生什么变化。游戏中的场景虽然是一座公园，但它所承载的想象，并不需要玩家真的拥有一片后院才能理解。
与此同时，团队也在考虑，未来能否进一步拓展游戏的环境与文化表达，让不同地区的玩家都能找到更多熟悉的元素。
既然聊到了这里，我当然也没有放过最后一个问题：“未来有没有可能在游戏里加入一些中国元素？无论是建筑、装饰，还是中国特有的昆虫，我觉得都可以成为一种方向。”
他表示，团队一直很惊讶，也很感激《禁闭求生2》在中国获得的支持。因此，他们也希望能够在游戏中加入更多让中国玩家感到熟悉的内容。至于具体会是什么，目前还没有可以公开的细节。
不过，他还透露了一个更明确的计划：随着游戏迈向 1.0 正式版，团队将会为游戏增加中文语音。
这项工作不仅是为了让玩家少读一些文本，更是希望大家能够直接听到角色的声音，让自己更自然地沉浸在这个世界里。
我突然想到了他的“Mr.Dips”的身份，赶忙问道，“等等，这个消息是第一次对外透露吗？”
Marcus又笑了，拍着我的肩膀说到：“对，这个就算是特意透露给你的独家新消息吧。”
采访结束时，我再次向 Marcus 表达了自己对《禁闭求生2》的喜爱，也希望黑曜石团队未来能够继续带来更多让人找回童年、重新发挥想象力的作品。
对于《禁闭求生2》来说，新的地图、新的昆虫、新的 Boss，以及越来越丰富的建造系统，当然都是游戏持续发展的重要部分。但对我自己而言，这款游戏最特别的地方，是它能让一个已经长大、每天忙于工作的人，再次沉浸式地想象：如果自己变得像蚂蚁一样渺小，眼前的世界又会变成什么模样。更意外的是，这份想象还可以与身边最亲近的人一同分享，最终成为两个人共同拥有的回忆。
而这正是 Marcus 和他的团队希望实现的目标：无论是第一次接触游戏的孩子，还是已经长大成人、偶尔怀念童年的玩家，都能在这个被放大的世界里，重新拾起那份熟悉的好奇心，开启一场属于自己的大冒险。
或许，这也是《禁闭求生2》能够跨越文化与年龄的界限，让不同地方的玩家找到共鸣的原因。
毕竟，人总会长大，但只要好奇心还在，属于自己的冒险就永远不会结束。
